concept.body: Tool dispatch: read what's GIVEN. A right angle → plain trig ratios or Pythagoras. A side matched with its opposite angle → Law of Sines. Two sides with the included angle (SAS), or three sides (SSS) → Law of Cosines. For area with two sides and the included angle: Area = ½·a·b·sin C.

explanationVariants: Three sides and no angles is SSS — the Law of Cosines solved for cos C.
Only Cosines digests three sides: cos C = (a² + b² − c²)/(2ab).

widget.prompt: You know all three sides of a triangle and want an angle. Which tool?

options.label: Law of Cosines, solved for cos C
options.feedback: SSS is Cosines territory: cos C = (a² + b² − c²)/(2ab), then inverse-cos.

options.label: Law of Sines, needing a known angle first
options.feedback: Sines needs at least one known angle to anchor a pair — SSS has none yet. Start with Cosines.

options.label: SOH-CAH-TOA, needing a guaranteed right angle
options.feedback: Without a guaranteed right angle the plain ratios don't apply. SSS → Law of Cosines.

options.label: Area = ½·ab·sin C, needing an angle already
options.feedback: The area formula CONSUMES an angle; it can't find one. Solve cos C from the Law of Cosines.

steps.body: One last gift from sine: **area without a height.** Any two sides a, b and their included angle C give Area = ½·a·b·sin C — because b·sin C IS the height on base a. At C = 90° it collapses to the familiar ½·leg·leg. No altitude to measure, ever.

explanationVariants: Half the product of the sides, scaled by the included sine: ≈ 28.28.

widget.prompt: Two sides measure 8 and 11, meeting at 40°. Area (2 decimals)?

commonErrors.feedback: 56.57 = 8·11·sin 40° forgets the ½ — that's the PARALLELOGRAM on those sides. The triangle is half: ≈ 28.28.
44 = ½·8·11 drops the sine — correct only if the sides met at 90°. Scale by sin 40°: ≈ 28.28.
33.71 = 44·cos 40° grabs cosine — but the HEIGHT is b·sin C, the opposite-style leg. ≈ 28.28.

steps.body: You now hold four tools. The dispatch rule reads the GIVENS: a right angle present → SOH-CAH-TOA (or plain Pythagoras). No right angle, but a side matched with its opposite angle → Law of Sines. Two sides hugging an angle, or all three sides → Law of Cosines. The givens choose the tool — you just read them.

widget.prompt: A triangle has angles 48° and 67°, and the side between... opposite the 48° is 21. No right angle. Best tool for the remaining sides?

options.label: Law of Sines — 21 and 48° make a matched opposite pair
options.feedback: A side with its opposite angle anchors the sine proportion; the third angle (65°) comes free from 180°.

options.label: Law of Cosines — the two stated angles choose it
options.feedback: Cosines wants two sides (SAS or SSS) — here only ONE side is known. The matched pair points to Sines.

options.label: SOH-CAH-TOA — the stated angles make a right triangle
options.feedback: The plain ratios need a right angle, and 48 + 67 = 115 leaves 65° — no 90° anywhere. Sines.

options.label: Pythagorean theorem — the 21-length side is given
options.feedback: Pythagoras is strictly right-triangle equipment. With a matched side-angle pair, the Law of Sines runs the show.

widget.prompt: New triangle: sides 13 and 19 with the 74° angle BETWEEN them. Best tool for the third side?

options.label: Law of Cosines — this is SAS
options.feedback: Two sides and the included angle plug directly into c² = a² + b² − 2ab·cos C.

options.label: Law of Sines
options.feedback: Neither known side faces a known angle — the 74° faces the UNKNOWN side. No matched pair, no Sines. Cosines.

options.label: Area formula ½·ab·sin C
options.feedback: That computes AREA, not a length. For the third side of SAS, the Law of Cosines.

options.label: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1
options.feedback: The Pythagorean identity relates one angle's ratios — it can't produce a side. SAS calls for Cosines.

explanationVariants: With a right angle present, plain tangent is fastest: x = 24·tan 31° ≈ 14.42.
The big laws still work, but SOH-CAH-TOA does it in one line: 24·tan 31° ≈ 14.42.

widget.prompt: A RIGHT triangle: the leg adjacent to the 31° angle is 24. The opposite leg (2 decimals)?

commonErrors.feedback: 39.94 = 24 ÷ tan 31° divides — the unknown opposite rides on TOP of tan 31° = x/24. Multiply: ≈ 14.42.
12.36 = 24·sin 31° casts the 24 as a hypotenuse — it's the adjacent LEG. Tangent: ≈ 14.42.
20.57 = 24·cos 31° mixes cosine into a two-leg problem. Leg-to-leg is tangent: ≈ 14.42.

explanationVariants: Dropping a height from the end of side b onto base a makes a right triangle where the height = b·sin C.
Height is the side OPPOSITE C in that little right triangle, with b as hypotenuse: h = b·sin C.

widget.prompt: In Area = ½·a·b·sin C, the factor b·sin C is really:

options.label: The triangle's height above base a
options.feedback: The altitude from b's far end makes a right triangle: h = b·sin C, so ½·base·height = ½·a·(b·sin C).

options.label: The length of the third side
options.feedback: The third side needs the Law of Cosines (with a −2ab·cos C term). b·sin C is the perpendicular HEIGHT.

options.label: Half the perimeter
options.feedback: Perimeter never enters this formula — b·sin C is a single perpendicular drop: the height on base a.

options.label: The projection of b along a
options.feedback: The along-a projection is b·COS C — the adjacent-style piece. The perpendicular piece, b·sin C, is the height.

steps.body: The whole course in one plot.
hints: Two sides with their included angle — the area formula's exact diet.
Area = ½·6·10·sin 30°, and sin 30° = ½ from the 30-60-90 ratios.
explanationVariants: Area = ½·6·10·sin 30° = 30 × ½ = 15 — exactly, thanks to sin 30° = ½.
Half of 60 is 30; the sine halves it again: 15.

widget.prompt: A triangular garden bed has sides 6 m and 10 m meeting at 30°. Its exact area in m²?

commonErrors.feedback: 30 = ½·6·10 stops before the sine — that's the area if the sides met at 90°. Scale by sin 30° = ½: 15.
25.98 = ½·6·10·cos 30° swaps in cosine — the height is b·SIN C. With sin 30° = ½: 15.
60 = 6·10 is the full sides-product — missing both the ½ and the sine: ½ × 60 × ½ = 15.

steps.body: Read the givens; they name the tool.
takeaways: Right angle → SOH-CAH-TOA / Pythagoras. Matched side-angle pair → Law of Sines. SAS or SSS → Law of Cosines.
Area = ½·a·b·sin C — the included sine builds the height for free.
Every tool here is similarity's child: the angle fixes the ratio, and the ratio measures the world.
steps.teaser: Course complete — next in the trail: circles, where these angles start turning.
